A Niggun of the Alter Rebbe
This niggun is not sung on Shabbos (אבינו מלכנו is not sung on Shabbos — whether as a niggun on its own, or as part of the Rosh Hashana tefillos). So, since Yom Tov falls on Shabbos and Sunday this year, enjoy singing this niggun at your second-day Yom Tov seuda!
At the Tzivos Hashem rally on Chof-Vav Elul תשמ״א‎ (1981), the Rebbe requested that all the chayolim sing this niggun together.

The Awe-some Niggun

"My neshama's trembling!" she whispers to her bubby.

"And it leads us to truly feel that Hashem is our father and king," Tatty adds.

Bubby nods. "Mine, too. The Eibishter seems so close."

As the last notes linger in the room, sixteen-year-old Mendel explains the meaning of the niggun. "Do you know why this niggun was sung during the Rebbe's tefillos of Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur? Because it's the Alter Rebbe's niggun. When

"By the end of the niggun, I felt that!" exclaims Bubby. "I'm sure that through our teshuva He will grant us a sweet new year."
